classification.difficultyReason: Construct right-triangle models from words, including a plan view for the sideways cannon miss, distinguish horizontal and sloping distances, and reconcile units before selecting ratios.

content.prompt: For the following questions, you will need to draw your own diagrams.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
A ladder rests against a wall. The foot of the ladder is 355 cm from the wall, and the ladder makes an angle of $63^{\circ}20'$ with the ground.
Calculate the length of the ladder to the nearest cm.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ be the ladder length. The horizontal distance is adjacent to the given angle.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 63^{\circ}20'&=\frac{355}{L}\\L\cos 63^{\circ}20'&=355\\L&=\frac{355}{\cos 63^{\circ}20'}\\L&\approx791\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution triangle: horizontal ground, vertical wall and ladder hypotenuse; schematic, not to scale.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent side 355 cm, ground angle 63 degrees 20 minutes, unknown hypotenuse L.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied student diagram.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
A glider is flying at an altitude (height) of 1.5 km.
To land, it descends at an angle of $18^{\circ}$ to the ground.
How far must the glider travel before landing? Answer rounded to the nearest 0.1 km.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the distance travelled along the descent path. The altitude is opposite the $18^{\circ}$ angle.
$$\begin{align*}\sin18^{\circ}&=\frac{1.5}{s}\\s\sin18^{\circ}&=1.5\\s&=\frac{1.5}{\sin18^{\circ}}\\s&\approx4.9\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution diagram showing the descending flight path as the hypotenuse and the altitude as a dashed perpendicular.
spec.mathematics: Opposite side 1.5 km, ground angle 18 degrees, unknown descent path s.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied student diagram.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
The entrance to the school is 60 cm above ground level.
A wheelchair ramp is to be built at an angle of $4^{\circ}$ to the ground.
How far horizontally from the school entrance must the ramp start? Answer to the nearest cm.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the horizontal distance from the school entrance.
$$\begin{align*}\tan4^{\circ}&=\frac{60}{x}\\x\tan4^{\circ}&=60\\x&=\frac{60}{\tan4^{\circ}}\\x&\approx858\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution ramp triangle, vertically exaggerated for readability; not to scale.
spec.mathematics: Rise 60 cm, ramp angle 4 degrees, unknown horizontal run x.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied student diagram.

children.label: d
children.prompt:
An aircraft is at an altitude of 770 m. It is 1.5 km horizontally from the airport.
What angle must it descend by to land safely? Answer to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
The horizontal distance is $1.5\text{ km}=1500\text{ m}$. Let $\theta$ be the angle of descent to the horizontal.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{770}{1500}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{770}{1500}\right)\\\theta&\approx27.171\ldots^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The minutes are $60\left[\tan^{-1}(\frac{770}{1500})-27^{\circ}\right]\approx10.27'$, so $\theta\approx27^{\circ}10'$.

spec.description: Authored descent triangle; the angle at the airport equals the descent angle to a horizontal through the aircraft.
spec.mathematics: Vertical altitude 770 m, horizontal distance 1500 m, unknown angle theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied student diagram.

children.label: e
children.prompt:
A cannon on level ground shoots at a target, but the shot misses sideways by 25 m, measured perpendicular to the line from the cannon to the target.
If the target is 1 km away, through what angle must the cannon's direction be adjusted?
Answer to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
Use a plan-view right triangle. The target distance is $1\text{ km}=1000\text{ m}$. Let $\theta$ be the required direction adjustment.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{25}{1000}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{25}{1000}\right)\\\theta&\approx1.432\ldots^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The minutes are $60\left[\tan^{-1}(\frac{25}{1000})-1^{\circ}\right]\approx25.93'$, so $\theta\approx1^{\circ}26'$.

spec.description: Authored plan-view triangle showing a perpendicular sideways miss; transverse dimension exaggerated for readability, not to scale.
spec.mathematics: Target distance 1000 m, perpendicular sideways miss 25 m, direction adjustment theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied student diagram.
